task: Owner report: Settings -> Certificates renew fails. portal renewCertificate merge-patched spec.renewBefore to 1s; the cert-manager webhook rejects it (renewBefore must be greater than 5m0s), it would not trigger renewal anyway, GitOps selfHeal would revert the drift, and the portal ServiceAccount had no patch/update on certificates; the error was swallowed into a bare 500. Switch to the cmctl renew mechanism (Issuing condition on the status subresource) with a minimal RBAC grant.

events.summary: renewCertificate GETs the Certificate, upserts the Issuing condition (status True, reason ManuallyTriggered, observedGeneration, lastTransitionTime) preserving other conditions, and PUTs /status exactly as cmctl pkg/renew/renew.go (v2.6.2) does with UpdateStatus; one re-read on 409. Never writes spec. ClusterRole narwhal-portal gets only update on cert-manager.io certificates/status (D-CERT-RENEW-ISSUING). The route authz gate (requireRole cluster-admin), idempotency and audit are unchanged; k8s 403/404/409/422 now map to meaningful responses and the error status is logged without bodies. Deliberately left alone: pre-existing behaviour that a failed renewal leaves the Idempotency-Key claim pending, and the post-renewal read-back pending/converged logic.

Server dry-run of the old merge patch against the live cluster returned spec.renewBefore: Invalid value: 1000000000: certificate renewBefore must be greater than 5m0s; kubectl auth can-i showed the portal SA could get but not patch/update certificates.
evidence: runtime:kubectl --context narwhal apply --dry-run=server of spec.renewBefore 1s -> webhook rejection

events.summary: Implemented the status-subresource renewal in portal/src/lib/k8s-client.ts, mapped k8s errors in the route, added the certificates/status update rule to the portal ClusterRole, and added k8s-client.renew.test.ts plus route.test.ts cases asserting a PUT to /status with an Issuing condition, other conditions kept, spec byte-equal, and 403/404/422 mapping.

events.scope: unit and static: pnpm typecheck, lint, test, build; LIVE on the local cluster (2026-11-04): RBAC applied via scripts/gitops/push-to-gitea.sh, renewal executed with the portal SA identity. NOT covered: the in-cluster portal pod itself (the dev image push to Harbor failed twice with a 502 on the NFS-backed registry, so the route was exercised from a local build with AUTH_MOCK against kubectl proxy impersonating system:serviceaccount:devtools:narwhal-portal), the real Keycloak login path, the 403-from-k8s mapping live.
evidence: runtime:kubectl auth can-i update certificates --subresource=status as the portal SA -> yes; update/patch certificates -> no
